lead: you have kept it to the letter for nineteen years, and the letter is the visible half. what the household stands on is a decision taken alone one winter, in an hour with no witness, described to nobody since.
sun: the covering goes over your own end of the agreement. what the two of you are inside is a going concern with meals in it, and how it is being held up has never been offered to the person holding the other end. they promised somebody they can describe in one sentence. you have let the sentence stand nineteen years, because correcting it and taking the covering down are the same afternoon.
moon: an undertaking made here needs no topping up. it came through the year neither of you liked the other, and the stretch where nothing was owed either way, because what was entered was an agreement rather than a mood, and nothing in you supplies a procedure for leaving one. the marriage is safe on one point of contact: your willingness to go on holding a thing nobody can check.
pull: they are standing on your end of a promise they have never been shown. it will outlast affection, it has already outlasted several years of it, and it gives no notice whatever if it goes.
tension: you get held up as the example, asked to speak at other people's weddings, cited by people deciding whether to bother. what cannot be said in that room is that the arrangement runs one way in the only place it matters: their promise went to a version of you that has never been produced, and yours is doing the work of both ends. every answer you give about how it was done is true and leaves the asker with nothing.
cost: the obligation does not decay on its own, which is why it was still being paid through an illness and through a stretch when the other person was unreachable. that same arrangement cannot be inspected from underneath, so the day the one decision goes, it goes with no leaning stage first, and the person who lived under it longest hears about it last.

lead: the list in the depot office runs by start date and no date on it is earlier than yours. every quarter you choose first, in public, and the sheet has never carried one word about what the choosing is for.
sun: a man whose wife is on treatment needs his days, so the days go to him and the run that starts at four in the morning goes to you, and what the paperwork records is a preference. they see somebody senior who likes nights. the arrangement keeping three households where they need to be exists in one head, and has no copy anywhere in that building.
moon: seniority here is arithmetic and checkable: a date, in a register, anybody can read and nobody can dispute. it also runs one direction. every person on that floor came in after you, so you can put a covering over any of them, and there is nobody above you to put one over you, overrule a pick, or carry a quarter when the four o'clock starts costing more than it did.
pull: your place at the top is a date anyone can look up. what it buys goes out on other people's rosters, and the same position guarantees nothing comes back the other way.
tension: the younger ones read the list as a queue you are sitting on, and say it where you can hear. straightening that out means naming which of them is being carried and why, on a floor where the naming would follow him until he leaves. so the resentment stands, exact about the sheet and wrong about every reason under it, and the one man who worked out what the picks were doing retired six years ago.
cost: three households have had a decade of ordinary weeks arranged around them by somebody who never once raised it, and no process that company runs could have arranged it at all. it sits on a date staying at the top of a list. the morning a medical goes against you, everybody moves up a number, the picks re-sort inside a week, and three families find out in the weather.

lead: the minutes of the last three meetings that place held are in a box in your house. two people who came out of the same place live here, and the box has never been mentioned to any of them.
sun: the people you house came out of the same place you did, and part of what the shelter keeps off them is the finding. the version they hold — bad luck, a man in an office who signed something — lets a person say where they grew up without it costing the evening. nothing you turned up has been produced for them, and the house is arranged around their never having to meet it.
moon: the digging did not stop at the cause, because nothing here issues a signal that a thing has been understood enough. it went on into the people, then into your own reason for leaving, and then into the shelter. you cannot inspect a support without taking it partly up, and there is one support. that work gets done at night, with the two of them asleep on the other side.
pull: you went all the way down into where you came from, and the bottom of a thing is nowhere anybody can be housed. the finding sits under a covering you keep testing by hand.
tension: it gets called dwelling on it, and from outside it looks like somebody who cannot leave a dead town alone. what has never been shown to anyone is that the question was answered years ago and the answer held; what continues is the checking of the answer, a different appetite wearing the same coat. meanwhile the two of them repeat the story you took apart, at your table, on an ordinary evening, and you pass the potatoes.
cost: you had the real cause of that closure inside a fortnight of the box arriving, sitting under three explanations everybody else finds sufficient, and two people at your table are somewhere better for it. examining a thing and dismantling it are one act here, and the object permanently under examination is the single support of the shelter those two sleep in.

lead: two hundred of them come in one door inside ten minutes and go out of it inside ten, and you move in that tide both ways, doing something in the middle of it the hall has no idea is happening.
sun: the ones you pick out get taken under: a number handed over quietly at the end of a row, a room offered for a fortnight, a standing arrangement nobody in that gathering has heard of, five people currently living on the strength of it. the place keeps no record of any of it. you arrive with everybody and leave with everybody, and somebody accounted for by a crowd is the best cover on offer.
moon: The Flock sorts, and sorts fast: a month in a room and you can name which five of two hundred are in real trouble, off posture, off who they arrive beside, off what has stopped being mentioned. nobody asked for the reading and the reading is right, and it runs on lives that were never handed over to be assessed. you are in that crowd weekly and never inside it.
pull: you come and go in the same tide as two hundred others, and five of them are dry tonight because of a judgement you made in silence and have reported to no one.
tension: they have asked you onto the committee twice and been turned down twice, which reads as a pleasant regular who does not want the commitment. the commitment is heavier than anything on their rota and will not go on a rota, since putting it there means naming the five and how they were chosen. so you get filed as somebody of no particular weight by a room holding every piece of the evidence and has never had it pointed out.
cost: somebody in real trouble gets picked out across a crowded hall inside a month, before any process there would have a form open, and two people are still here on the strength of that speed. the sorting and the housing are one person, renewed weekly by your walking in. a season away does not thin it out, it stops it, on a tuesday, with the hall registering nothing missing.
